target_claim: The proof asserts that the least element ⊥ of a Boolean algebra "is contained in every filter" (used to conclude that the family 𝓕_a of filters containing a is nonempty). This is false: ⊥ lies in a filter only if that filter is the whole algebra, so no proper filter contains ⊥. A closely related load-bearing claim on line 0039 ("if 𝓕 is a proper filter containing a, then 𝓕 is not maximal") is refuted by the same kind of finite witness.
source_quote: Since $B$ is a Boolean algebra, it has a least element $\bot$, which is contained in every filter.
